established:

   C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – MAY 2021

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2020-21 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 20-30 dated June 16, 2020) and California Government
  Code §53646, the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the
  City Council, City Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The May
  2021 Cash and Investment Report is presented to receive and file in
  accordance with the City’s adopted 2020-21 Investment Policy.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for May 2021.

  D. CORRECTIVE ACTION PLAN TO THE COMPLETED STATE AUDIT

  As required by the California State Auditor, City staff has prepared a corrective
  action plan for the twelve recommendations documented in the audit report.
  The corrective action plan is due to the California State Auditor by June 26,
  2021.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the report.

  E. ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 21-27 APPROVING THE FISCAL YEAR
  2021/2022 SENATE BILL 1 (SB1) ROAD REPAIR AND ACCOUNTABILITY
  ACT PROJECT LIST

  Senate Bill 1, also known as the Road Repair and Accountability Act of 2017,
  provides the City of San Gabriel with funds for basic road maintenance,
  rehabilitation, and safety projects. In Fiscal Year 2021-2022, the City must
  adopt a list of eligible street improvement projects. This item adopts the
  project list and authorizes the Public Works Director to file the required
  documents with the California Transportation Commission. Approval of
  Resolution No. 21-27 will allow the City to receive SB1 funding estimated by
  the State of California to be $770,410 for Fiscal Year 2020-2021.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 15, 2021  3
   1. Adopt Resolution No. 21-27; and
  2. Authorize the Director of Public Works to file necessary documentation to
  satisfy SB1 funding requirements and act as the signature authority.

  F. AGREEMENT FOR USE OF SMITH PARK POOL BY SAN GABRIEL SEA
  GULLS

  On June 30, 2021, the Agreement between the City of San Gabriel and the
  San Gabriel Sea Gulls for the use of Smith Park Pool will expire. The San
  Gabriel Sea Gulls (SGSG) use Smith Park Pool for their regular swim team use.
  The SGSG uses the pool throughout the year for its swim team practices and
  swim meets. There is no cost to the City in that the hourly rate covers the cost
  of pool personnel and utility expenditures. Based on a typical-use year and
  the proposed hourly rate, the estimated revenue for Fiscal Year 2021-2022
  will be $45,500.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Agreement for San
  Gabriel Sea Gull’s use of Smith Park Pool to be effective immediately and
  ending June 30, 2022, and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  agreement.

  G. AGREEMENT FOR USE OF SMITH PARK POOL BY MID VALLEY WATER
  POLO

  On June 30, 2021, the Agreement between the City of San Gabriel and Mid
  Valley Water Polo for the use of Smith Park Pool will expire. Mid Valley Water
  Polo (MVWP) has had use of Smith Park Pool since October 2020 for their
  regular water polo team practices. There is no cost to the City in that the
  hourly rate covers the cost of pool personnel and utility expenditures. Based
  on a typical-use year and the proposed hourly rate, the estimated revenue for
  Fiscal Year 2021-2022 will be $29,250.

  Recommended Action:
  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Agreement for Mid Valley
  Water Polo’s use of Smith park Pool to be effective immediately and ending
  June 30, 2022, and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 15, 2021  4
   H. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 21-28, RELATED TO PERMANENT
  LOCAL HOUSING ALLOCATION (PLHA) YEAR 2 FUNDING AND
  PROPOSED ELIGIBLE ACTIVITIES

  The Los Angeles County Department Authority (LACDA), on behalf of Los
  Angeles County and its participating cities, will be applying for funding for
  Year 2 of the Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA) Program from the
  California Department of Housing and Community Development. The
  allocation is based on real estate recording fees, and it is estimated that the
  City of San Gabriel will be allocated $292,199 from the $17 million grant for
  the period July 1, 2021 – June 30, 2022 (Year 2). The City of San Gabriel has
  the opportunity to utilize this funding opportunity toward eligible housing
  activities as identified in the PLHA grant guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-28, which
  approves the following actions:

  1. Elect the following eligible activities, subject to the State approval, for
  Year 2 of the 5-year PLHA grant period:

  (1) The predevelopment, development, acquisition, rehabilitation, and
  preservation of multifamily, residential live-work, rental housing that is
  affordable to extremely low-, very low-, low-, or moderate-income
  households, including necessary operating subsidies.

  (3) Matching portions of funds placed into Local or Regional Housing
  Trust Funds.

  2. Allocate, upon State approval, $261,929 of the Year 2 PLHA allocation
  toward eligible activity #1, and $30,270 toward eligible activity #3 to renew
  the City’s affiliate membership to the San Gabriel Valley Regional Housing
  Trust (SGVRHT) and for use as capital funds by SGVRHT to support affordable
  housing in the region; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute new contracts with LACDA for the
  5-year PLHA Plan grant period and for Year 2 of the allocation, and make
  adjustments as necessary to reflect the actual allocation of funds to San
  Gabriel.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 15, 2021  5
   Alternatives

  The City Council may want to consider alternative activities for Year 2 of the
  5-year PLHA Plan grant period, which can include the following:

  1. Elect a different eligible activity other than staff’s recommendation.

  2. Elect a combination of different eligible activities.

  I. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH WILLIAM HEZMALHALCH
  ARCHITECTS (WHA) FOR ARCHITECTURAL, URBAN DESIGN, AND
  HISTORIC PRESERVATION PROFESSIONAL SERVICES

  On January 4, 2021, the City of San Gabriel issued a Request for Proposals
  (RFP No. 21-01) for a qualified firm to provide architectural, urban design, and
  historic preservation professional services. The City received six proposals and
  William Hezmalhalch Architects (WHA) best met the criteria outlined in the
  RFP.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve the Professional Services Agreement with William Hezmalhalch
  Architects (WHA);

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute said agreement; and

  3. Issue a purchase order in the amount of $40,000.

  The City Council will hold a Public Hearing to consider adoption of the
  Proposed Operating Budget, Capital Improvement Plan (CIP), Appropriations
  Limit and Fee Schedule for Fiscal Year 2021-22. The operating budget is
  balanced, with revenues totaling $81,196,446 and expenditures totaling
  $67,261,477. The General Fund is also balanced, with $48,191,860 in revenues
  and $43,876,659 in expenditures. The CIP totals $21,396,700, for 27 projects,
  utilizing a combination of new revenues and existing fund balances. The
  Appropriations Limit is calculated at $46,355,277. The Proposed Fee Schedule
  requires amendments to the San Gabriel Municipal Code, which are proposed
  in Ordinance Nos. 672 and 673, which will be introduced for first reading.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council conduct a public hearing on the
  Proposed 2021-22 Operating and Capital Improvement Program Budgets, Fee
  Schedule and related Ordinances, and Appropriations Limit, and after
  receiving comments and testimony adopt the following resolutions:

  Resolution No. 21-22 adopting the City of San Gabriel Fiscal Year 2021-22
  Operating Budget;

  Capital Improvement Program Budget;

  A. DRAWDOWN OF CALPERS OPEB RETIREMENT TRUST

  The City has established a California Employer’s Retirement Trust with
  CalPERS (OPEB Trust) to provide funding for employee retiree health costs.
  Since Fiscal Year 2008-2009 funds have been deposited into the OPEB Trust.
  The funds in the OPEB Trust can only be used to pay employee retiree
  healthcare costs. A drawdown from the OPEB Trust will improve the General
  Fund’s fund balance and cash position. A drawdown will reduce the balance
  in the OPEB Trust and increase the OPEB liability.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council direct staff to drawdown $600,000
  from the OPEB Trust to pay a portion of retiree healthcare costs incurred
  during the fiscal year.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 15, 2021  8
   B. OPTIONS FOR THE PUBLIC WORKS YARD LOAN

  In December of 2014, the City borrowed $7.8 million from Citizens Business
  Bank (CBB) for the construction of the Public Works maintenance facility. The
  City was required to provide collateral for the loan in the form of a 10-year
  certificate of deposit for the loan amount. The General Fund cash used as
  collateral for the loan is restricted. Due to the cash restrictions, the General
  Fund has had to borrow cash from other City funds. City staff has been
  soliciting offers to refinance the loan to improve the General Fund’s cash
  position. Due to the City’s financial condition and being listed as a high-risk
  city by the California State Auditor, offers to refinance the loan have been
  limited. The City has received an offer to refinance the loan. The loan offer
  and the current loan terms are presented and analyzed for City Council
  consideration.

  Recommended Action:

  Due to the $402,000 increase in debt payments, the low interest rate on the
  Public Works Loan, the higher interest rate on the Royal Business Bank Loan,
  and the projected improvements to the General Fund’s cash and fund balance
  position, staff recommends that the City Council hold steady with the current
  Public Works Loan.

  Alternatives

  A. Hold steady with the Public Works Loan and direct staff to continue to
  solicit offers to refinance the Public Works loan, potentially through a
  bond issuance.

  B. Move forward with the Royal Business Bank Loan at the proposed terms.

  C. HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS AND RELATIONS (HEAR) COMMISSION 2021
  PROPOSED ANNUAL WORKPLAN

  The Annual Workplan developed by the Human Equity, Access and Relations
  Commission is intended for the 2021 calendar year. The Commissioners have
  had open and constructive dialogue to develop a plan that best fits in
  alignment with the goals and scope of the HEAR Commission as well as the
  City of San Gabriel’s Mission.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 15, 2021  9
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and approve the HEAR
  Commission’s Annual Workplan for 2021.

  D. DISCUSSION ON RE-OPENING OF CITY FACILITIES TO THE PUBLIC AND
  THE TIMING OF RETURNING TO IN-PERSON CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS

  Since the spring of 2020, when the COVID-19 pandemic began, City facilities
  have been open to the public by appointment only and City Council meetings
  have been held virtually. Beginning on July 6, 2021, City facilities will reopen
  to the public for walk-in service. The City Council directed staff to place an
  item on the agenda to talk about the timing of returning to in-person City
  Council meetings.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss the proposed social distancing
  and safety protocols and direct staff on when to schedule in-person City
  Council meetings.

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, July 6, 2021, at
